question.text: Nearly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the power of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>110</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> light bulb is converted to visible radiation. The change in average intensities of visible radiation, at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the bulb to a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math>' will be

solution.text:
Power of visible radiation is P'=10100×110 W =11 W

Change in average intensity of visible radiation is  ∆Iradiation=Iradiation1-Iradiation2

⇒I1-I2=P'4πr12-P'4πr22

=114π11-125  =114π×2425

=264π×10-2=84×10-2 W m-2

Hence, the value of a=84.
